title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 142 (Guarantee obtained by misrepresentation invalid)

content.overview: Section 142 provides that any guarantee which has been obtained by means of misrepresentation made by the creditor, or with his knowledge and assent, concerning a material part of the transaction, is invalid.
content.glance: A guarantee obtained by misrepresentation by the creditor (or with his knowledge and assent) concerning a material part of the transaction is invalid.
content.study: Any guarantee which has been obtained by means of misrepresentation made by the creditor, or with his knowledge and assent, concerning a material part of the transaction, is invalid. Current-law framing: the misrepresentation must concern a material part and be by or with the knowledge and assent of the creditor.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Any guarantee which has been obtained by means of misrepresentation made by the creditor, or with his knowledge and assent, concerning a material part of the transaction, is invalid.

examples.title: Material misrepresentation by creditor
examples.body: Creditor misrepresents a material fact to induce the guarantee. The guarantee is invalid under Section 142.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor knowingly allows a material misrepresentation to be made to the surety. Is the guarantee valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 142 invalidates a guarantee obtained by misrepresentation made by the creditor or with his knowledge and assent concerning a material part.
